chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I supplicate and desire to weep, but it does not come to me, and sometimes I remember some of my family who have died, so I lose sleep and weep. Is that permissible?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. Remember them, and when your heart is softened, weep and supplicate to your Lord, Blessed and Exalted.'
ai.seo_question: How should one approach weeping during supplication if they do not naturally feel like crying?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the spiritual practice of inducing tears during supplication (*du'a*) as a means of deepening humility (*khushu*). He instructs the believer to actively recall deceased loved ones to soften the heart, highlighting the Shia emphasis on emotional engagement and remembrance of death (*dhikr al-mawt*) as a catalyst for divine connection.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I tend to supplicate and am desirous for the weeping, be it does not come to me, and sometimes I remember someone from my family who had died, so I cannot sleep and I weep. So is that allowed for me?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. When you remember them and cannot sleep and weep, so supplicate to Your<sup>azwj</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘When I pray and plead before Allah for help, I like to weep but it does not come through, but if I recall members of my family who have died I may feel weeping. Is that permissible?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, it is permissible. When you recall them and feel like weeping then pray to your Lord, the Most Blessed, the Most High.’”
